title: LOGIC: Learning Optimal Goals with an Integrated Critic for Generative Auto-Bidding

problem.claim: Decision Transformers face difficulty specifying optimal Return-to-Go targets and lack exploration beyond the offline dataset.

gap.claim: Prior studies addressed the two challenges separately, but their solutions introduced new problems.

contributions.claim: LOGIC is a unified framework that addresses optimal-goal specification and exploration in offline learning.
LOGIC uses an integrated critic to guide a generator toward discovering high-value Return-to-Go goals instead of exploring at the action level.
The Backward Consistency Refinement module operates during training and inference to maintain mathematical and semantic validity of generated plans.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on diverse auto-bidding scenes reportedly show that LOGIC significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
The authors report superior cumulative returns and model robustness for LOGIC.

narrative_sequence.summary: Offline Decision Transformers have target-specification and exploration deficiencies.
Existing attempts addressed the deficiencies separately and created additional problems.
LOGIC unifies the solution by guiding goal discovery with an integrated critic and generator.
The framework explores beyond the dataset frontier and applies BCR to preserve plan validity.
Experiments in diverse auto-bidding scenes report improved baseline performance, cumulative returns, and robustness.

source_observation.claim: The framework shifts exploration from actions to high-value goals and uses an integrated critic to guide goal generation.

interpretation.claim: When action-level exploration is difficult in offline learning, exploring over structured intermediate objectives may provide a more tractable search space.

application.claim: Consider critic-guided generation of target objectives or Return-to-Go values in offline sequential decision systems.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy transfers beyond the reported auto-bidding scenes.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark datasets, baseline identities, or quantitative performance values.
The abstract does not describe the critic, generator, or Backward Consistency Refinement implementation details.
The abstract does not establish independent verification or reproducibility.
